pages.text: "That neck is too thin. I can make it better!" Gaga, who knew best, lifted Duri's snow duck. But crumble—the neck broke off.
Careless Duri's eyes filled with tears. "I worked on it so long..." Gaga stretched their neck, then quickly turned away. "I... I did not do it."
Gaga went away and packed snow alone. However firmly Gaga pressed, the duck's neck kept breaking. Only cold wind rushed through the yard.
Duri crouched beside the broken duck. Gaga felt as if a stone lay on their chest. Heavy and uncomfortable, Gaga could not even pack snow.
Teacher Bau stopped clearing snow and crouched beside Gaga. "Gaga, a stone is resting on your chest. How can we put it down?" Gaga only fiddled with a snowball.
"Broke it? Say sorry!" Teacher Bau said softly. "Those words take the stone away." Gaga breathed deeply out.
Gaga went before Duri, looked straight at them, and said, "Duri, I broke your duck. I am sorry." The stone in Gaga's chest melted away.
Duri scooped up snow and shared it with Gaga. "Then let us make one together!" Four hands shaped one duck. A snow duck with a thick neck stood in the yard.
The next day, Gaga accidentally stepped on Duri's mitten. Opening both palms, Gaga said at once, "Sorry! One, tell right away if I break something! Two, say sorry! Three, make it again together!"
Duri put an arm around Gaga's shoulders. One sorry made the heart light again. Patting the snow duck, Gaga said, "Broke it? Say sorry!"
